rubber_generalization.description: Rubber: train on uniaxial tension + equibiaxial tension, test on pure shear. Comparing SI-CANN (fixed α+=2) vs GI-CANN (learned α+*). This is the core claim for rubber: GI-CANN discovers α*≈1.675 and achieves near-perfect R².

r2_ut.description: Uniaxial-tension R2 on the evaluated slice.

r2_bt.description: Equibiaxial-tension R2 on the evaluated slice.

r2_ps.description: Pure-shear R2 on the evaluated slice.

avg_r2.description: Mean R2 across all deformation modes in this experiment.

avg_normalized_rmse.description: Average RMSE normalized by each mode's stress range; catches poor magnitude fit even when R2 is high.

tail_normalized_mae.description: Average absolute error at the largest-deformation evaluated row, normalized by stress range.

shape_violation_rate.description: Fraction of adjacent evaluated intervals where prediction trend reverses the observed stress trend.

alpha_star.description: Reported learned or fixed exponent for interpretability auditing; zero coefficient avoids rewarding paper-value matching.

rubber_negative_ablation.description: Rubber with negative exponent (I₂-like behavior). Shows that negative exponents perform poorly for rubber — an ablation confirming that stretch-dominated materials prefer positive exponents.

brain_generalization.description: Brain cortex: train on uniaxial tension + uniaxial compression, test on simple shear. Comparing SI-CANN (fixed α-=-2) vs GI-CANN (learned α-*≈-18). This is the core claim for brain tissue: GI-CANN discovers a large negative exponent capturing shear-sensitive behavior.
